lines.text: Well a pleasant autumn evening to you folks tuning in across Wisconsin and wherever else you might have us on the wireless. This is Bob, and we are right here at American Family Field for the start of the World Series. Tampa Bay and Milwaukee. Game one of the fall classic. Nick Martinez gets the ball for the visitors, and Jacob Misiorowski takes the mound for our boys. Grab a seat on the porch.

Nick Martinez takes the ball for Tampa Bay tonight, thirty-six years old out of Miami with a big-league career stretching all the way back to twenty-fourteen. They call him Tricky, and I will tell you, back in my catching days in the low minors, anybody throwing that many years would have struck me out twice before I even dropped my doughnut . And for our boys, young Jacob Misiorowski gets the call. Just twenty-four, born out in Missouri, standing six-foot-seven on the mound.
One ball, zero strikes. Yandy Díaz takes a look at the four-seamer from Misiorowski, 104, just over the plate. That’s a quiet start to the top of the first.
Yandy Díaz swings at the four-seam fastball, 102, right down the middle — that one cuts through the air like a slice of pie. Count now stands 1 ball, 1 strike.

Misiorowski fires another hundred-mile-an-hour four-seamer, Díaz lifts it deep toward right, Frelick drifts back and hauls it in for the first out of the inning, and we are still scoreless here in the top of the first.

Jonathan Aranda takes a look at that 103-mph four-seam from Misiorowski — straight up the middle, no frills. That one just clipped the strike zone, making it 0 balls, 1 strike. Quiet start to the top of the first.

With one out and two aboard in a scoreless first, Misiorowski looks in, deals a ninety-six mile an hour cutter and Caminero lines it right to third base for a double play, Hamilton to Turang, and that wraps up the top of the inning with no score on the board!

Well that brings us out of the top half with no runs on two hits for Tampa Bay, leaving us dead even at zero all. Folks, when you visit Milwaukee you simply have to see the Racing Sausages dash along the warning track, a beloved local tradition since the nineties. Time now for the Brewers to swing the bats in the bottom of the first.

Martinez works quick, fires a ninety-one mile an hour cutter, and Chourio lines it safely to right fielder Victor Mesa Jr. for a single. Nobody out, runner on first, still no score here in the bottom of the first inning.

Bauers steps up, nothing on the board yet, and just before he swings, there's a pickoff attempt from first — a quick move, a step back, a flick of the glove — but the ball doesn't come down. Still, the count holds at zero, zero, and the inning keeps rolling.
Martinez fires a ninety-one mile an hour cutter, Bauers takes a look, swings clean — ball, count now 1 and 0. Quiet start, just like the way the Brewers always begin a game, slow and steady.

Fastball, 95, fouled off, count still 2 and 2. Bauers stands there, calm as ever. Martinez keeps it tight, like he’s been doing since the first pitch. Just another one of those nights when the game starts slow and stays that way.

Jake Bauers stands there, calm as ever, just like that night in ’18 when I tried to catch a fly ball in the stands and missed it entirely. Still no run, just like the way the game starts slow and stays that way.

Well that brings our first frame to a close with Milwaukee jumping out in front by two to zero on three hits. Tampa Bay got a couple themselves earlier, but they are still looking for their first score as we turn things over to the top of the second.

Let us take a short breather and see what the top of the third brings us.
